I'm actually less concerned about war than I am the stock market. High frequency trades have already done enough to completely dissociate the value of the stock market from the actual worth of companies, and skim a constant supply of money off the top to further enrich the 1%. We don't need AI in the hands of bankers too.

With respect to war, I simply don't think the AI will ever truly have enough accurate data to properly learn war. In my cursory reading of war, it almost seems like the winner is just the side which doesn't fuck up the worst. Strategy and tactics are constantly evolving, and with every major conflict, conventional wisdom flies out the window as emergent properties of new technology are discovered in the field. And the most bizarre, unlikely, downright insane things can turn a battle, which landslides into millions of other consequences. But who knows.

You know, actually, thinking on it further, the AI might have one sure fire application in war. Logistics. Learning the most efficient way to send the precise amount of resources needed to the places they are needed through the best routes. That sort of data is plentiful, and predictable.
